items.label: Stop
items.title: Stop focusing on winning, regardless of relationship support

items.label: Observe
items.title: Identify the source of discomfort first, then back off

items.label: Start

items.completion_signal: Complete the action once and record whether subjective load changed afterward.

items.label: Stop

resolved_copy.gloss: How do you make internal associations and possible deductions outside of realistic information.
resolved_copy.daily_meaning: When the score is high, it is easier to see pictures and assumptions in unformed clues; when the score is low, it is more reliant on proven facts and processes.
resolved_copy.why_it_matters: It affects whether you first expand the possibilities when understanding complex problems, or first compress them to the boundaries of executable reality.

resolved_copy.gloss: Your sensitivity to form, atmosphere, rhythm and detailed texture.
resolved_copy.daily_meaning: High scores are usually more quickly affected by the quality of space, language, images, or sounds; low scores are less likely to allow aesthetic cues to change the focus of judgment.
resolved_copy.why_it_matters: It explains why some people are affected by the "unclear but not right" texture, while others are more concerned about whether the function is established.

resolved_copy.gloss: Are you willing to identify, access and express your inner feelings.
resolved_copy.daily_meaning: High scores are more likely to use emotions as a source of information; low scores are more likely to put feelings aside and return to tasks and facts.
resolved_copy.why_it_matters: It determines whether feelings are incorporated into judgments or downplayed as background noise.

resolved_copy.gloss: Are you willing to correct yourself with new practices, routes and experiences?
resolved_copy.daily_meaning: Those with high scores are more likely to try it themselves; those with lower scores are more likely to stick to familiar solutions until there is sufficient evidence for a new solution.
resolved_copy.why_it_matters: It affects whether openness stays at the understanding level or whether it actually enters behavioral experimentation.

resolved_copy.gloss: Your interest in abstract concepts, systematic relationships, and interpretive frameworks.
resolved_copy.daily_meaning: A high score will naturally ask about the underlying mechanism; a low score will pay more attention to whether the conclusion is directly usable.
resolved_copy.why_it_matters: It explains why a person makes the effort to understand the "why" rather than just the "how."

resolved_copy.gloss: The extent to which you can adjust to established rules, traditional positions, and value boundaries.
resolved_copy.daily_meaning: High scores are more willing to re-examine old rules; low scores are more in need of stable principles and inheritable boundaries.
resolved_copy.why_it_matters: It affects whether you first loosen your stance when faced with new ideas, or whether you first confirm whether it undermines the core order.

resolved_copy.gloss: A basic sense of your ability to handle tasks, understand requirements, and solve problems.
resolved_copy.daily_meaning: High scores will make people more willing to take on complex responsibilities; low scores will make people more likely to need more confirmation and support before starting.
resolved_copy.why_it_matters: It determines whether you first feel "I can dismantle it" or "I'm not sure I can hold on" when faced with a request.

resolved_copy.gloss: Your need for structure, tidiness, planning, and predictability.
resolved_copy.daily_meaning: High scorers will proactively establish lists, rules, and sequences; low scorers are more tolerant of on-the-fly adjustments and loose structures.
resolved_copy.why_it_matters: It explains why some people rely on order to regain control, while others lose flexibility in excessive order.

resolved_copy.gloss: Do you keep commitments, rules and obligations at the forefront of your decision-making?
resolved_copy.daily_meaning: High scores are more likely to place "should be done" seriously; low scores are more likely to be reordered by situational value.
resolved_copy.why_it_matters: It affects whether a person is pulled by responsibilities or more easily able to renegotiate commitments from changes in needs.

resolved_copy.gloss: Your drive for goals, standards, and upward achievement.
resolved_copy.daily_meaning: Higher scorers report striving for better results more often; lower scorers may be more willing to stop at good enough.
resolved_copy.why_it_matters: It determines whether conscientiousness is driven by results or just maintains basic operations.

resolved_copy.gloss: Your self-reported tendency to begin and continue tasks despite distraction or a lack of immediate reward.

resolved_copy.why_it_matters: It explains why a person may be stuck in executing a goal despite clearly understanding it.

resolved_copy.gloss: Your tendency to evaluate risks, consequences, and steps before taking action.

resolved_copy.why_it_matters: It explains that fatigue is sometimes not a lack of motivation, but a mismatch in rhythm.

resolved_copy.gloss: Your need for fresh, intense, and high-arousal experiences.

resolved_copy.why_it_matters: It affects whether you view stimulation as fuel or as a load to be managed.

resolved_copy.gloss: The frequency with which you naturally experience and express feelings of lightness, excitement, and pleasure.

resolved_copy.why_it_matters: The score alone cannot tell whether a person feels less enjoyment, expresses it less, or experienced a different context.

resolved_copy.gloss: You assume that others’ intentions are trustworthy and that relationships allow for goodwill first.

resolved_copy.why_it_matters: It affects how quickly a collaboration begins and how you handle uncertain interpersonal risks.

resolved_copy.gloss: You tend to be direct, transparent, and non-strategic in expressing your ideas.
resolved_copy.daily_meaning: High scores tend to speak clearly; low scores consider timing, interests, and information retention.
resolved_copy.why_it_matters: It explains whether a person speaks sincerely or is more accustomed to speaking as a matter of relationship management.

resolved_copy.gloss: Do you naturally take other people's situations, needs, and burdens into consideration.

resolved_copy.why_it_matters: It affects whether you will automatically bear additional care costs during the cooperation.

resolved_copy.gloss: Your tendency to maintain relationships, give in, and avoid escalation during disagreements.

resolved_copy.why_it_matters: It affects whether you prioritize error prevention before action, or whether you allow action itself to generate answers.

resolved_copy.gloss: The extent to which you unleash feelings of kindness, closeness, and accessibility in one-to-one interactions.

resolved_copy.why_it_matters: It can distinguish between two things: whether it requires crowd stimulation and whether it can create a warm connection.

resolved_copy.gloss: Your natural preference for group company and participation in group interaction.

resolved_copy.gloss: Do you naturally occupy the expressive position, make demands and influence the direction of the context?

resolved_copy.why_it_matters: It affects whether one's ideas will enter external systems in time.

resolved_copy.gloss: Your preferred pace of life, density of tasks, and level of physical energy.

resolved_copy.why_it_matters: It explains that fatigue is sometimes not a lack of motivation, but a mismatch in rhythm.

resolved_copy.why_it_matters: It affects whether you view stimulation as fuel or as a load to be managed.

resolved_copy.gloss: The frequency with which you naturally experience and express feelings of lightness, excitement, and pleasure.

resolved_copy.why_it_matters: It affects how quickly a collaboration begins and how you handle uncertain interpersonal risks.

resolved_copy.gloss: You tend to be direct, transparent, and non-strategic in expressing your ideas.

resolved_copy.gloss: Are you willing to lower your prominence and avoid putting yourself at the center?

resolved_copy.action_bridge: Track both the completion signal and the recovery cost, not output alone.

items.title: Condensing complexity into a decision-making problem
items.body: If you tend to consider several explanations in a discussion, finish by writing down the one decision question that matters now, the available evidence, and what is still missing. Record whether this helped the discussion; the score itself does not establish understanding.

items.why_recommended: The matched work evidence points to a start or structure gap, so a low-cost action can produce fast feedback.
items.completion_signal: Complete one minimum action in the stated time frame and record whether starting became easier.

items.label: Stop
items.title: Stop silently swallowing excess load
items.body: When it becomes clear that a task, relationship, or rhythm is taking a toll on you, don't continue to keep the cost internally.
items.why_recommended: The current work pattern may maintain output through avoidable load; removing one cost amplifier is more sustainable.
items.completion_signal: Interrupt the old habit once and record whether the result actually became worse.

items.label: Observe
items.title: Keep track of the types of meetings that consume you the most
items.body: Record for two consecutive weeks: Which meetings are most likely to put you into high load early, whether it is because of vague goals, unclear responsibilities, or repeated pulling.
items.why_recommended: The evidence is better suited to identifying the real conditions behind work pace before changing it.
items.completion_signal: Record three tasks and distinguish the conditions linked to flow and slowdown.

items.label: Continue
items.title: First name the need, then talk about right and wrong
items.body: Continue to translate high somatosensory into understandable needs, such as my need for clearer timing, boundaries, or responses, rather than jumping straight into who is right and who is wrong.
items.why_recommended: If you already use this approach and have observed helpful effects, consider retaining it. Otherwise, first examine when it fits.
items.completion_signal: After two interactions, identify how the practice improved understanding or boundaries.

items.label: Start
items.title: Tell me your true thoughts first
items.body: Before you are ready to continue to remain silent, say something true but not necessarily complete, so that there is an entrance in the relationship that can continue to catch you.
items.why_recommended: The matched evidence reveals a small opening in expression or feedback; a reversible trial fits better than a wholesale style change.
items.completion_signal: Make one clear, respectful, reversible expression and record the other person's actual response.

items.label: Stop
items.title: Stop focusing on winning, regardless of relationship support
items.body: When you have made your point clear, don't continue to push the other person into a defensive position; first make sure the other person can still catch it.
items.why_recommended: The current pattern may push conflict, accommodation, or expression costs too high; pausing one automatic reaction can reduce misreading.
items.completion_signal: Recognize and pause the old reaction once before responding.

items.label: Observe
items.title: Identify the source of discomfort first, then back off
items.body: When you want to withdraw directly, first mark whether the discomfort comes from being misunderstood, having boundaries touched, or from an increased sense of loss of control.
items.why_recommended: Relationship behavior depends heavily on person and context, so observing differences is more useful than assigning a label.
items.completion_signal: Record the person, context, feeling, and response in three interactions and identify a repeated pattern.

items.label: Start
items.title: Start 10-minute disengagement recovery
items.body: Every time you clearly feel that the load is being stretched, physically disengage for 10 minutes first, and do not continue to carry it while exerting pressure.
items.why_recommended: The matched evidence supports addressing load early with a low-effort, reversible action.
items.completion_signal: Complete the action once and record whether subjective load changed afterward.

items.label: Stop
items.title: Notice whether repeated scrolling interrupts recovery
items.body: Observe how repeatedly checking messages affects your tension. If it adds strain, try a brief pause and compare how you feel; do not assume the same approach helps in every setting.
items.why_recommended: The current pattern may let stimulation or rumination occupy recovery space; removing one amplifier is more direct than adding another task.
items.completion_signal: End one stress-amplifying input or loop and record whether recovery began sooner.

items.label: Observe
items.title: Compare expected cost to actual cost
items.body: Record for two consecutive weeks: What is the bad outcome you are worried about and what is the cost of it actually happening, to help the system return to the facts from the rehearsal.
items.why_recommended: Recovery improves when triggers, peaks, and decline are separated; the evidence supports establishing a personal baseline first.
items.completion_signal: Record the trigger, peak, and recovery duration for three stress events.

items.label: Continue
items.title: Reserve meaningful exploration time
items.body: Continue to reserve time for exploration that allows you to understand the world, renew your experiences, or form new connections, but give it a clear boundary.
items.why_recommended: If you already use this approach and have observed helpful effects, consider retaining it. Otherwise, first examine when it fits.
items.completion_signal: At the end of the period, identify one small, repeated, verifiable improvement.
